title: Drug use disorders and substance-induced psychosis
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's substance use disorder.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for maintenance therapy.

Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 74, SpO2 98% on room air, Temp 98.6 F, Weight 205 lbs.

Recent Labs:
eGFR: 88 mL/min/1.73m2
HbA1c: 5.8%
WBC: 7.2 x 10^9/L
Platelets: 240 x 10^9/L

Medication List:
- Buprenorphine 16mg sublingual daily
- Multivitamin daily

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Negative for fever, chills, fatigue.
Neurological: Negative for tremors, dizziness.
Psychiatric: Negative for anxiety, depression.
Respiratory: Negative for shortness of breath, cough.
Gastrointestinal: Negative for nausea, abdominal pain.
Musculoskeletal: Negative for joint pain.

Social History: Lives with spouse and two children. Works as a construction supervisor. Denies any recent substance use.

Family History: Father had hypertension. Mother had type 2 diabetes.

Family History: History of hypertension and diabetes in parents.

HPI: Patient is a 51-year-old male who presented for management of opioid use disorder. He has been on a stable maintenance regimen. Patient reports consistent adherence to the prescribed buprenorphine. He reports feeling stable and productive at work. He states he has remained in remission for a period of 5 months without any cravings or return to use.

Exam:
General: Alert and oriented x3. Well-groomed and in no acute distress.
Psychiatric: Cooperative, normal affect, congruent mood. Speech is clear and coherent.
Physical: Lungs clear to auscultation. Heart sounds regular and and S1, S2 present. Abdomen soft, non-tender. Extremities are intact with no edema.

Assessment:
1. Opioid use disorder, severe. The patient is currently in early remission and has maintained stability for 5 months on buprenorphine.

Plan:
1. Continue current buprenorphine maintenance dose.
2. Continue to monitor for any signs of relapse.
3. Follow up in 3 months for routine check.

Electronically signed, J. Lindqvist, NP, 05/14/2026
explanations: Severe opioid use disorder in early remission: opioid dependence, in remission, F11.21 (HCC 137).

hccs.label: Drug Use Disorder/Moderate/Severe/Drug Use with Non-Psychotic Complications
